input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI codes are stripped, the code also calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text, removing leading and trailing whitespace. Prompts such as `"Name: "` lose their trailing space.
- rationale: Trigger: prompt text ends in a space (click builds prompts as `text + suffix`, with the default suffix `": "`) and the stream is not a tty or color is disabled. In that case the stripping branch runs and `.strip()` removes the trailing space, so the user's input is typed directly after the colon (`Name:foo`). It also changes output compared with echo-based prompting, which only strips ANSI. This is visible in CliRunner tests and with piped output.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation as the label: a `.strip()` call made after removing ANSI codes, which drops the trailing space of `'Name: '` when color is not supported (non-tty, CliRunner, piped output). That leaves the input glued to the colon. Mechanism and trigger are identical.
